text:
vikram: FYI hit a weird case during a canary today — console rollout set 10/90 but runtime flag on the service seems to be sending 100% to v1. anyone seen this?

maria: hmm, can you paste the request that hit the runtime flag path?

vikram: pasted below. service owner said they set a runtime flag via our Admin API earlier this morning.

vikram: ```json
{"user_id":"u-123","route":"/generate","runtime_flags":{"force_variant":"v1"}}
```

josh: oh, that's the crux. we currently have two signal sources: the Console rollouts (console UI -> rollout-policy store) and the runtime flags coming from the internal admin API. precedence is murky.

sarah: agreed. historically platform doc said "runtime overrides console for emergency fixes" but I can't find an authoritative precedence table. docs are inconsistent.

maria: that matches what I remember — runtime flags were intended as emergency kills/overrides for teams, but we never formalized which guards (quota/split) get re-evaluated after an override.

vikram: result is user-visible skew during the canary. product PM noticed traffic split not matching experiment.

josh: is this the same behavior for guard checks? example: console rollout has a guard that blocks 10% if quota_exceeded=false. If runtime flag sets variant, do we skip the guard?

sarah: currently code path is: evaluate guards -> consult console policy -> consult runtime flag -> apply variant. but applyVariant() can short-circuit metrics/tags which breaks experiments. implementation detail, not policy.

maria: so we have two layers of issues: 1) policy ownership/intent (who should win) and 2) implementation that causes side-effects when runtime flags are applied.

josh: proposal: surface 'origin' in both the API and console UI. when a request is routed, annotate which source decided variant (console|runtime|fallback). then dashboards/telemetry can show divergence.

vikram: +1. that would make debugging much easier. also need a canonical precedence doc for platform->service owners. I can draft a short matrix.

sarah: actionable items:
- add origin tag to routing events (telemetry)
- add visible badge in Console rollout UI: "overridden by runtime flag"
- write precedence matrix and publish to eng-platform docs

maria: technical followups: we should stop short-circuiting metric tagging when runtime flag forces variant. metrics must always record the guard checks and the source.

josh: minimal API change: expand route evaluation result: `{ "variant":"v1","source":"runtime","guards": ["quota_ok"] }`

vikram: will that be backward-compatible? some infra code expects just variant string.

sarah: yes if we add a new header X-Routing-Origin and keep the variant body the same for now. increment API minor version for the enriched response.

maria: quick patch idea (pseudocode):
```js
function decideVariant(req) {
  const guardOk = runGuards(req);
  const consoleChoice = consultConsole(req);
  const runtimeChoice = consultRuntime(req);
  // current impl short-circuits metrics when runtimeChoice exists
  // new impl: always record guards and then pick precedence per policy table
  recordGuards(req, guardOk);
  const final = precedenceTable.pick(consoleChoice, runtimeChoice, fallback);
  return { variant: final, source: provenance(final) };
}
```

josh: we should also be explicit about which signal owners can set what:
- Console rollouts: owned by product/platform (experiments, scheduled rollouts)
- Runtime flags (admin API): owned by service teams and SRE for emergencies
- Protecting guards (quota, compliance): owners defined per guard, usually platform

vikram: can we put a short note in Console UX where people create rollouts: "If a runtime flag exists with higher precedence, the rollout may be overridden. Click to see active overrides."

maria: UX note: show active overrides inline with a hover tooltip linking to the admin API audit log entry.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout-service v2 -> v3 (canary 10%) by maria @ 1938759200 :rocket:

vikram: ok actionable summary:
1) I will draft a precedence matrix doc and share by EOD.
2) Maria will add origin header + telemetry patch (small API bump).
3) Sarah will add Console badge and link to audit logs.
4) Josh will coordinate with service owners to confirm runtime-flag intended semantics.

maria: i'll open PR for telemetry change and include a migration note.

josh: can we also add a lint/check in rollout creation that warns if there's a known runtime-flag present for the same service? just a soft warning initially.

vikram: love that. prevents accidental experiment misconfig.

sarah: thanks everyone. let's treat this as high-priority for the next sprint — experiments must be reliable. :white_check_mark:
